task: A user with a huge number of packfiles (tens of thousands) reports that even `git rev-parse --short HEAD`, which their shell prompt runs all the time, went from about 0.4s to 4.5s after upgrading. Has this been seen before, and what causes it?
gold: Adding packs to the packfile store (packfile_store_add_pack / packfile_list_append) first scanned the whole existing list (packfile_list_remove_internal) to check whether the pack was already there, making loading N packs O(N^2); a regression since packs moved into the packfile store
The fix adds a fast path that skips that already-in-list check for packs known to be new (the append function gained an explicit parameter to skip the check)
It is already fixed (commit e4621a0169 or equivalent statement), with a perf test in t/perf/p5303-many-packs.sh

task: `git clone --revision=refs/heads/main <url>` segfaults against one of our older servers, but works fine against GitHub. It also crashes if I force `-c protocol.version=0`. What is going on?
gold: With protocol v0 the server advertises all refs including HEAD, so remote_head_points_at is non-NULL but its peer_ref is NULL (with v2 only the requested ref comes back and remote_head_points_at is NULL, so the code is skipped)
update_remote_refs() in builtin/clone.c dereferences remote_head_points_at->peer_ref->name, which segfaults
The fix adds a check that remote_head_points_at->peer_ref is non-NULL before that block (already fixed, 1034ad383f)

task: Running `git merge-file --object-id ...` inside a linked worktree dies with `BUG: ... cannot reinitialize an already-initialized object directory`. It works in the main worktree. Why?
gold: merge-file runs with RUN_SETUP_GENTLY so the repository is already set up, but with --object-id it called setup_git_directory() again, a redundant second setup
In a linked worktree that calls repo_set_gitdir() twice, which used to be silently accepted but became a BUG after a change to handle changing a repository's commondir (odb)
The fix only calls setup_git_directory() when there is no repo (if (!repo && object_id)), keeping the correct 'not a git repo' error outside a repository

task: `git log -L` combined with `-G` (or `-S` / `--find-object`) hits an assertion failure on a file that was renamed at some point in its history. Is this known, and what causes it?
gold: line-log's queue_diffs() passed the caller's diff_options, including the user's pickaxe options, into rename detection (diff_tree_oid / diffcore_std), so diffcore_pickaxe discarded diff pairs needed to detect the rename

The missed rename lets a later deletion pair through uncleaned to process_diff_filepair() with an invalid filespec, triggering the assertion (earlier versions silently truncated history at the rename)
The fix builds a private diff_options for rename detection inside queue_diffs(), the same pattern as blame's find_rename(), isolating it from user options

task: We keep getting zombie child processes when a git fetch over a remote helper or ssh is killed. Should we just set clean_on_exit on the transport-helper and connect child processes so git kills and reaps them on abnormal exit?
gold: It was tried (commit dd3693eb08) and reverted: when the child is run through a shell, git kills and waits for the shell, not the real process, so the zombie remains anyway with bash, dash, etc.

Some shells such as mksh wait for their children without propagating the signal, causing a deadlock (git waits on mksh, mksh on the child, the child waits on git's pipe); seen in t5702 with SHELL_PATH=/bin/mksh
It was a regression for mksh users and did not achieve the goal; the alternative is a cleverer approach or accepting zombies and letting PID 1 reap them

task: The newer multi-pack-index v2 format lifts the lexicographic pack ordering requirement. Should git write midx v2 by default?
gold: It was made the default and then reverted to v1: older Git (e.g. 2.53) does not ignore an unknown midx version but die()s, so a v2 midx written (possibly behind the scenes, e.g. during fetch) makes the repository unusable for older Git
The default now depends on the feature: v2 only when the requested feature needs it, such as midx compaction (git multi-pack-index compact); users can set midx.version
Mixed Git versions on the same repository is the case being protected

task: When `git multi-pack-index repack` builds its new pack, should it feed pack-objects with `--stdin-packs` instead of an object list, to get better delta compression?
gold: That was done (b7d6f23a171) and reverted: focusing on pack-files separates object selection from how the midx picks a single pack for an object that has copies in several packs
The delta-compression improvement can be had with the existing object list mechanism
An object walk at that point has further pitfalls in blobless partial clones that would need more testing

task: On one machine t9300-fast-import.sh hangs forever in the checkpoint tests, and the trace shows it reading `rogress checkpoint`, with the first byte missing. What is happening?
gold: It is a bug in Dash v0.5.13 (bisects to its multi-byte pmatch change; fixed upstream in v0.5.13.2), where the shell's read loses the first byte, not a git bug
The test waits for fast-import to print 'progress checkpoint' and never sees it, so it loops forever
The workaround rewrites the wait loop in background_import_then_checkpoint (collecting the output in a command substitution and testing it after), which does not trigger the bug

task: Our CI jobs on Ubuntu 25.10 images started failing at the sudo steps. Anything known about that?
gold: Ubuntu 25.10 defaults to the Rust sudo-rs, which does not support the --preserve-env flag that git's CI relies on
ci/install-dependencies.sh switches back to the C sudo with update-alternatives --set sudo /usr/bin/sudo.ws (when /etc/alternatives/sudo exists)

task: When a git command triggers auto maintenance, does it run in the background, what decides that, and does the test suite behave differently?
gold: It detaches by default, controlled by maintenance.autoDetach, falling back to gc.autoDetach when that is unset (prepare_auto_maintenance in run-command.c passes --detach or --no-detach)
When neither config is set, the GIT_TEST_MAINT_AUTO_DETACH environment variable decides (default true)
t/test-lib.sh sets GIT_TEST_MAINT_AUTO_DETACH=false, so maintenance runs synchronously in tests to avoid races
